# 🧩 TagKey

**TagKey** is a lightweight, strongly-typed identifier for entity tags. It wraps an integer ID generated by
[EntityKeyStore](EntityKeyStore.md), providing type safety and avoiding repeated string lookups at runtime.

---

## 🧩 Overview

Instead of passing string tag names everywhere, you can define `TagKey` instances once and reuse them. The key stores
the integer ID internally, so operations like `AddTag`, `HasTag`, and `DelTag` are fast and allocation-free.

```csharp
public static partial class GameEntityAPI
{
    public static readonly TagKey IsEnemy = new(nameof(IsEnemy));
    public static readonly TagKey<IGameEntity> IsSelectable = new(nameof(IsSelectable));
}
```

These keys can then be used with extension methods from `Extensions_Tags.cs`:

```csharp
entity.AddTag(GameEntityAPI.IsEnemy);
bool isEnemy = entity.HasTag(GameEntityAPI.IsEnemy);
entity.DelTag(GameEntityAPI.IsEnemy);
```

---

## 🔍 Variants

| Struct | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `TagKey` | General-purpose tag key for any [IEntity](../Entities/IEntity.md). |
| `TagKey<E>` | Tag key bound to a specific entity type `E`. Prevents accidental mixing between entity types. |

---

## 🗂 Examples of Usage

### Define Tag Keys in an API Class

```csharp
public static partial class GameEntityAPI
{
    public static readonly TagKey IsEnemy = new(nameof(IsEnemy));
    public static readonly TagKey IsBoss = new(nameof(IsBoss));
    public static readonly TagKey<IGameEntity> IsSelectable = new(nameof(IsSelectable));
}
```

### Use Extension Methods

```csharp
public static class GameEntityExtensions
{
    public static void MarkAsEnemy(this IEntity entity) =>
        entity.AddTag(GameEntityAPI.IsEnemy);

    public static bool IsEnemy(this IEntity entity) =>
        entity.HasTag(GameEntityAPI.IsEnemy);

    public static void MarkAsSelectable(this IGameEntity entity) =>
        entity.AddTag(GameEntityAPI.IsSelectable);
}
```

### Direct Use

```csharp
IEntity entity = ...;

entity.AddTag(GameEntityAPI.IsEnemy);

if (entity.HasTag(GameEntityAPI.IsEnemy))
    Debug.Log("Enemy detected!");

entity.DelTag(GameEntityAPI.IsEnemy);
```

## 🔍 API Reference

### TagKey

```csharp
public readonly struct TagKey : IEquatable<TagKey>
```

#### `TagKey(string)`

```csharp
public TagKey(string name)
```

- **Description:** Creates a tag key from a string name.
- **Parameter:** `name` — The tag name.

#### `TagKey(int)`

```csharp
public TagKey(int id)
```

- **Description:** Creates a tag key from an existing integer ID.
- **Parameter:** `id` — The numeric tag identifier.

#### `ToString()`

```csharp
public override string ToString()
```

- **Description:** Returns the original tag name via [EntityKeyStore.IdToName](EntityKeyStore.md).

### TagKey\<E\>

```csharp
public readonly struct TagKey<E> : IEquatable<TagKey<E>> where E : IEntity
```

Same API as `TagKey`, but bound to entity type `E`.

---

## 📌 Best Practices

- Define tag keys once in a static API class and reuse them.
- Use `TagKey<E>` when multiple entity types exist in the same project to catch type mismatches at compile time.
- Prefer keys over string names in hot paths to avoid repeated `EntityKeyStore.NameToId` lookups.
- Keep tag names stable — changing a name changes the generated ID unless a deterministic algorithm is used.
